channel.title: The Daily Digest
channel.description: One top story from each of my chosen publications, updated daily.

item.title: NYT: Who Will Win the Midterms? Republicans Are Reeling.
item.description: The party is putting up a costly defense of states and districts that President Trump won easily in 2024. And in places like Georgia, strategists wonder if it’s too late.

item.title: NPR: Greetings from Beijing, where baozi are worth the wait in line
item.description: The popular fluffy steamed buns are filled with pork, vegetables, tofu — and in one trendy Beijing shop, chocolate and red beans.

item.title: BBC News: Remains found after wildfire identified as mother-of-three missing since 2019
item.description: A 56-year-old man is arrested after the remains of Joanne Sheen were found in London almost seven years after she went missing.

item.title: The Guardian: ‘We left everything behind’: 125,000 people displaced as war reignites in Yemen
item.description: Fierce fighting has forced people to abandon their homes, leaving everything behind to seek shelter in refugee camps The rapid Houthi advance in Yemen: why it matters and what’s at stake Abandoning their homes and crammi…

item.title: Al Jazeera: Ghalibaf’s maths missile at Trump decoded: Is Iran fixing US interest rates?
item.description: Iran's speaker mocks US interest rates, citing the Taylor equation amidst rising global oil prices and inflation.

item.title: Ars Technica: Apple reportedly building server packed with M-series Ultra chips for AI
item.description: Planned 2029 debut could make this Apple’s first enterprise server in decades.

item.title: WIRED Backchannel: Why the Postpandemic Tech Bust Sent Billionaires to Trump
item.description: Following mass layoffs in 2022 and 2023, many tech workers turned against their employers. When liberal politicians also rallied against Silicon Valley, their backers turned to Donald Trump.

item.title: WIRED Science: The Trump Administration Sends a New Signal to Alien Disclosure Whistleblowers
item.description: The Defense Department issued a legal waiver authorizing current and former personnel to share unidentified anomalous phenomena–related classified information, but it doesn’t extend to other agencies.

item.title: WIRED Business: Flock Once Touted Its Cameras as ‘Made in the USA.’ Now It’s Not So Clear
item.description: Flock reveals little about where its license plate readers are assembled, but the answer could have geopolitical and cybersecurity implications.

item.title: The New Yorker: How, Exactly, Could A.I. Kill Us?
item.description: Employees of A.I. companies are increasingly sounding the alarm. What should we make of their warnings?

item.title: New York Mag The Cut: Travis Kelce Was Named As a Ponzi-Scheme Victim
item.description: Siddharth Jawahar allegedly stole $35 million from investors.

item.title: New York Mag Curbed: Paul Feig Is Selling His Very Colorful Lenox Hill One-Bedroom
item.description: The director is listing his prewar condo for just a little bit more than what he paid for it in 2017.

item.title: Fox59: ISP investigating fatal police shooting in Pulaski County
